newsitem.title: USA: CIA officer to plead not guilty as spy for Moscow.
newsitem.headline: CIA officer to plead not guilty as spy for Moscow.

text.p: Harold Nicholson, the Central Intelligence Agency officer arrested on Saturday, will plead not guilty to charges of conspiracy to commit espionage on behalf of Moscow, Nicholson's lawyer said on Wednesday.

"He will plead not guilty," the court-appointed lawyer, Jonathan Shapiro, said in a telephone interview with Reuters. Shapiro said he would ask the judge, at a scheduled hearing on Monday, to release Nicholson pending trial.
Shapiro said he would argue for bail to be set for Nicholson or whatever other guarantees the court might seek to ensure that "he's not going to flee, which he is not."
Nicholson, 46, a 16-year veteran of the clandestine service, is a former CIA station chief and the highest-ranking CIA official to be formally charged with spying for Russia.

The government has accused him of selling secrets to Moscow for at least the past two years for at least $120,000 in cash. He is being held without bail in a city jail in Alexandria, Virginia, a Washington D.C. suburb.

Shapiro declined to discuss what advice he was giving Nicholson about cooperating with investigators from the CIA and the Federal Bureau of Investigation trying to assess the damage he did to U.S. intelligence sources and methods.
